data.content_ref: inline:The target's distinction between 'risk-minimization' and 'induction' collapses because any strategy that prefers Theory A over Theory B based on past test results necessarily assumes that the conditions which made A superior in the past will remain relevant or operative in the future application context. Popper explicitly rejected the principle of the uniformity of nature; therefore, acting on corroboration without assuming some continuity between past performance and future reliability is logically incoherent. The claim that one can treat corroboration merely as a 'record of error-elimination' while using it to guide future action smuggles in the very inductive assumption (that eliminated errors are indicative of future stability) that the argument claims to avoid.
